sm: Calley Means, speaking with Joe Rogan, describes who he says runs the White House. He claims chief of staff Susie Wiles holds the tightest control over policy of any chief of staff in modern history, with deputies including James Blair, Walker Barrett and Richard Walters, plus pollster Tony Fabrizio. He says these figures have long careers taking money from industries such as pharmaceuticals, pesticides, sugar and Pepsi, and that this shaped decisions on school lunch reform and defining ultra-processed food. He also says lobbying firms tied to the relatives of Wiles and campaign manager Chris LaCivita, and Ballard Partners, saw revenue surge. He stresses he doesn't think President Trump knows most of this.

Means says the problem is structural and bipartisan, pointing to Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries, whose former staffers are also becoming lobbyists. He says Fabrizio told him MAHA was not a big part of the strategy, which centered on redistricting and raising money for the midterms. He says the political team pushed messages like no tax on tips and affordability, while polls show Americans name corruption as the top issue. Rogan and Means discuss an article saying Wiles shut down talk of oversight probes and insisted they would win. Means says staffers are now trying to blame the president, though he agrees Trump holds ultimate responsibility.
